```{=html}
<div style="text-align:center; margin:0.6em 0 1.4em; font-family:'Cormorant Garamond',serif; font-size:1.85em; color:#F5E9C4; font-style:italic; font-weight:300; line-height:1.35;">
```

## Data & Feature Engineering {background-color="#000000"}

```{=html}
<div class="two-col">
<div>
<h3>Dataset v2</h3>
<ul>
  <li><strong>1,440 rows</strong> — 24 Lartisien-verified hotels, 6 room tiers, 10 sample dates</li>
  <li>Preliminary EDA removed 2 IQR outliers (Cheval Blanc, The Brando) from 26 hotels</li>
  <li>Missing values (hotel room count only) filled with per-hotel <strong>median</strong>, not mean — robust to skew/outliers in a small per-hotel sample, and this column isn't even used by the final model anyway</li>
  <li>Target 1: <strong>is_premium</strong> (rate > €3,000/night)</li>
  <li>Target 2: <strong>log_rate</strong> → back-transform via expm1()</li>
  <li>80/20 stratified split · StratifiedKFold(5) clf · KFold(5) reg</li>
</ul>
<div class="box" style="margin-top:1em;">
  <div class="box-title">Leakage Prevention</div>
  <div class="box-body">All preprocessing inside scikit-learn Pipeline — StandardScaler + OHE fitted on X_train only. Cross-validation uses inner folds on train only. Test set untouched until final evaluation.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div>
<h3>7 Engineered Features (v2 — interpretable)</h3>
<table>
  <tr><th>Feature</th><th>Rationale</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Type of Room (Deluxe → Presidential)</td><td>Primary driver — 44% reg importance</td></tr>
  <tr><td>Room Type — Extreme vs. Middle</td><td>Nonlinear Presidential premium</td></tr>
  <tr><td>How Exclusive Is the Hotel? (1–3)</td><td>Replaces 23 brand OHE dummies</td></tr>
  <tr><td>Which Month? (two seasonal waves)</td><td>Cyclic — Dec/Jan are neighbours</td></tr>
  <tr><td>How Close to Christmas?</td><td>Smooth spike near 25 Dec</td></tr>
  <tr><td>Is It School Holiday Season?</td><td>French school calendar demand</td></tr>
  <tr><td>What Kind of Resort Is It?</td><td>beach/city/island/lake/mountain</td></tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
```

## Feature Collinearity Check — VIF Audit {background-color="#000000"}

```{=html}
<div style="display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:20px;">

<div>
  <div style="font-size:0.65em; letter-spacing:0.18em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#C9A02C; margin-bottom:12px; font-weight:600;">Pairwise Correlations — Time Features</div>
  <table>
    <tr><th>Feature pair</th><th>r</th><th>Verdict</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Month wave 1 ↔ Month wave 2</td><td>0.116</td><td><span class="pill-good">✓ independent</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Month wave 2 ↔ Christmas closeness</td><td style="color:#E8C96A;">0.503</td><td><span class="pill-warn">moderate</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Christmas closeness ↔ school holiday</td><td>0.331</td><td><span class="pill-good">✓ acceptable</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Month wave 1 ↔ Christmas closeness</td><td>−0.097</td><td><span class="pill-good">✓ independent</span></td></tr>
  </table>

  <div style="margin-top:12px; font-size:0.65em; letter-spacing:0.18em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#C9A02C; margin-bottom:8px; font-weight:600;">VIF Scores (threshold: 10)</div>
  <table>
    <tr><th>Feature</th><th>VIF</th><th>Status</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Which Month? (wave 1)</td><td>1.10</td><td><span class="pill-good">✓ clean</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Which Month? (wave 2)</td><td>1.45</td><td><span class="pill-good">✓ clean</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>How Close to Christmas?</td><td>1.83</td><td><span class="pill-good">✓ clean</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Is It School Holiday Season?</td><td>2.31</td><td><span class="pill-good">✓ clean</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Type of Room</td><td>4.96</td><td><span class="pill-warn">moderate</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>How Exclusive Is the Hotel?</td><td style="color:#E8C96A;">6.66</td><td><span class="pill-warn">elevated — acknowledged</span></td></tr>
  </table>
</div>

<div>
  <div style="font-size:0.65em; letter-spacing:0.18em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#C9A02C; margin-bottom:10px; font-weight:600;">Why Do These Correlate? Real-Life Explanation</div>

  <div class="box" style="margin-bottom:10px;">
    <div class="box-title">Which Month? ↔ How Close to Christmas? (r = 0.503)</div>
    <div class="box-body">
      Both peak in <strong>December</strong>. The "which month" wave naturally hits its maximum on 1 December; Christmas closeness also maxes out in December. They partially overlap in what they "see." <br><br>
      <em>Why kept:</em> Christmas closeness captures the <strong>sharp, nonlinear spike</strong> in the final days before 25 Dec — it rises steeply. The month wave captures the <strong>broader winter season</strong> curve (also high in November, early Jan). VIF = 1.45 and 1.83 — model can still separate their contributions cleanly.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="box" style="margin-bottom:10px;">
    <div class="box-title">How Close to Christmas? ↔ School Holiday (r = 0.331)</div>
    <div class="box-body">
      December is both close to Christmas <em>and</em> a school holiday month. <br><br>
      <em>Why kept:</em> school holidays also cover <strong>July and August</strong> (summer peak), which are far from Christmas. The two features measure entirely different demand drivers — Christmas surge vs. family travel season.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="box">
    <div class="box-title">How Exclusive Is the Hotel? — VIF = 6.66, most elevated</div>
    <div class="box-body">
      This feature partially overlaps with resort type (e.g. island resorts tend to be the most exclusive tier). <strong>Acknowledged limitation.</strong> Still far better than 23 hotel OHE dummies (VIF >> 10). VIF &lt; 10 = acceptable for tree-based models which are robust to moderate collinearity.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

</div>
```

## Model Ladder — Classification {background-color="#000000"}

> **Task:** Predict *is_premium* (> €3,000/night) · **Metric:** F1-macro on held-out test set

```{=html}
<table>
  <tr><th>Model</th><th>CV F1</th><th>Test F1</th><th>ROC-AUC</th><th>Beat Dummy?</th><th>Overfit gap</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Dummy (majority class)</td><td>0.356</td><td>0.356</td><td>0.500</td><td><span class="muted">baseline</span></td><td><span class="pill-good">0.000</span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>Logistic Regression (C=1)</td><td>0.730</td><td>0.734</td><td>0.816</td><td><span class="pill-good">+0.378</span></td><td><span class="pill-good">0.007</span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>Decision Tree (full depth)</td><td>0.721</td><td>0.719</td><td>0.719</td><td><span class="pill-good">+0.363</span></td><td><span class="pill-warn">0.143 ⚠ OVERFITS</span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>Random Forest (n=300)</td><td>0.775</td><td>0.762</td><td>0.838</td><td><span class="pill-good">+0.406</span></td><td><span class="pill-warn">0.129</span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>GradBoost (max_depth=3)</td><td>0.812</td><td>0.804</td><td>0.905</td><td><span class="pill-good">+0.448</span></td><td><span class="pill-good">0.069</span></td></tr>
  <tr style="background:rgba(201,160,44,0.07);">
    <td><strong class="gold">XGBoost (tuned) ★ WINNER</strong></td>
    <td><strong class="gold">0.814</strong></td><td><strong class="gold">0.805</strong></td><td><strong class="gold">0.905</strong></td>
    <td><span class="pill-good">+0.449</span></td><td><span class="pill-good">0.064</span></td>
  </tr>
</table>
<div style="margin-top:0.8em; font-size:0.68em; color:#555; text-align:center;">
  Decision Tree overfits (Train F1=1.000 vs Test F1=0.719). Capping GradBoost/XGBoost at max_depth=3 corrects this. XGBoost: CV F1=0.814 ≈ Test F1=0.805 — genuine generalisation confirmed.
</div>
```

## Methodology Recap — Leakage, Independence, Overfitting, Metrics {background-color="#000000"}

```{=html}
<div class="two-col">
<div>
<div class="box" style="margin-bottom:10px;">
  <div class="box-title">1 · No Data Leakage</div>
  <div class="box-body">Train/test split happens first (80/20, stratified). StandardScaler + OneHotEncoder live inside a scikit-learn Pipeline and are fitted on X_train only — the test set is mathematically invisible until the final scoring step, for every model in both ladders.</div>
</div>
<div class="box" style="margin-bottom:10px;">
  <div class="box-title">2 · Independent Features (VIF + Correlation)</div>
  <div class="box-body">All 7 engineered features were run through a correlation matrix and VIF audit. Every feature scored VIF &lt; 10 (the standard threshold); the one elevated score (6.66) was investigated, explained, and kept deliberately — see the audit slide.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div>
<div class="box" style="margin-bottom:10px;">
  <div class="box-title">3 · How We Solved Overfitting</div>
  <div class="box-body">
    <strong>First</strong>, we tried to eliminate it directly: GradBoost was manually capped at max_depth=3 (regularisation); XGBoost's max_depth/n_estimators/learning_rate were found via a real GridSearchCV (12 combos × 5-fold CV) — which independently converged on the same values, validating the manual choice. Decision Tree's unconstrained gap (0.143) dropped to 0.06–0.07 for both.<br><br>
    <strong>Then</strong>, we recognised why the remaining risk matters less than it looks: this model only has to predict rates for the 24 known Lartisien Collection hotels, never an unseen brand — a narrower target than a general-purpose luxury-hotel model, which is part of why the small gap is credible.
  </div>
</div>
<div class="box">
  <div class="box-title">4 · Choosing the Right Metric</div>
  <div class="box-body">Classification target is imbalanced (~35/65) — accuracy would flatter Dummy (66%), so <strong>F1-macro</strong> is primary. Regression: <strong>MAE</strong> (€1,677) is the most business-readable, same-unit-as-target metric and is robust to the few very expensive Presidential Suite outliers; R² is kept as the technical cross-model comparison figure.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
```

## Key Findings {background-color="#000000"}

```{=html}
<div class="two-col">
<div>
<h3>What drives luxury pricing?</h3>
<div style="margin:0.6em 0;"><div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:0.72em;margin-bottom:3px;"><span class="gold">Type of Room (Deluxe → Presidential)</span><span class="muted">44%</span></div><div class="bar-wrap"><div class="bar-fill" style="width:100%;"></div></div></div>
<div style="margin:0.6em 0;"><div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:0.72em;margin-bottom:3px;"><span class="gold">How Exclusive Is the Hotel? (1–3)</span><span class="muted">13%</span></div><div class="bar-wrap"><div class="bar-fill" style="width:30%;"></div></div></div>
<div style="margin:0.6em 0;"><div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:0.72em;margin-bottom:3px;"><span class="gold">How Close to Christmas?</span><span class="muted">11%</span></div><div class="bar-wrap"><div class="bar-fill" style="width:25%;"></div></div></div>
<div style="margin:0.6em 0;"><div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:0.72em;margin-bottom:3px;"><span class="gold">Which Month? (seasonality)</span><span class="muted">12%</span></div><div class="bar-wrap"><div class="bar-fill" style="width:27%;"></div></div></div>
<div style="margin:0.6em 0;"><div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:0.72em;margin-bottom:3px;"><span class="gold">What Kind of Resort? (mountain/beach…)</span><span class="muted">7%</span></div><div class="bar-wrap"><div class="bar-fill" style="width:16%;"></div></div></div>
</div>
<div>
<h3>Honest Limitations</h3>
<div class="box"><div class="box-title">Tier Generalisation Is Limited — Use Within This 24-Hotel Set</div><div class="box-body">"How exclusive is the hotel?" has the highest VIF in the feature set (6.66) and each tier is built from very few hotels (10 / 8 / 6 hotels in tiers 1/2/3) — too small a sample to trust the tier score on a brand-new, unseen property. The train-test gap (0.06–0.07) was only ever measured on these 24 known hotels, never on a held-out new hotel. Because of this, the app should be read as valid for these 24 existing Lartisien Collection properties specifically, not as a general luxury-hotel pricing tool.</div></div>
<div class="box" style="margin-top:0.7em;"><div class="box-title">No Real-Time Rates</div><div class="box-body">Flash sales, last-minute deals, and year-over-year price inflation are not captured. Cross-sectional historical data.</div></div>
<div class="box" style="margin-top:0.7em;"><div class="box-title">Decision Tree Overfits</div><div class="box-body">Full Decision Tree: Train F1=1.000 vs Test F1=0.719 (gap=0.143). Capping GradBoost/XGBoost at max_depth=3 (gap=0.064) resolves this.</div></div>
</div>
</div>
```
